mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, proxied by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Significant negative 20-day forward returns when HOUST shows persistent downward trends over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, measured by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative even when PAYEMS shows consistent upward momentum over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to higher borrowing costs and reduced equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward returns during identified rate hike months (p > 0.10 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand or supply chain issues, which typically precede a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when INDPRO shows sustained declines over 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home prices (implied by low inflation and strong demand, CPIAUCSL < 2.0) generate optimism that drives a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0 without other demand indicators changing.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%) coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market expectations for corporate profits decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 6.5% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day forward returns when UNRATE remains above 6.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) and rising funds rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a conflicting signal that produces a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return when both conditions persist.
failure_condition: Rank IC > 0.05 over 60-day horizon when both proxies show the specified trends.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent industrial production declines (INDPRO < 110 for 3 months), the S&P 20-day forward return is more likely to be negative due to weak economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of INDPRO contraction periods (walk-forward split).
